note: Names, descriptions and grades are PlayStation's official list. Guides are written for this entry in our own words; each step names the source it draws on. Counts marked target are the numbers PlayStation tracks.

trophies.guide: The platinum pops on its own the moment the other 54 trophies are earned, so there is no separate task to chase. Treat it as the finish line of the roadmap below: story first, then partner crime, activities, side strands, collectibles, crime mastery, and the money cleanup last.
trophies.name: Vice Got a Price!

steps.text: Work the roadmap stage by stage, S1 to S7, and let the platinum unlock when the last trophy lands.
If one trophy is still missing, use the checklist filter by kind to see exactly which group it sits in.

trophies.guide: Gone Fishing is the opening mission, so this is the first story trophy most players earn and it cannot be missed. Play through the intro beats until the mission-complete screen appears.
trophies.name: Just Like Paradise

steps.text: Start a new game and follow the opening mission markers until Gone Fishing wraps up.
No side task is needed: finishing the mission itself unlocks the trophy.

trophies.guide: Chapter 1 closes once its last mission is done, so keep pushing the story markers and skip nothing the chapter asks for. This is also the chapter that holds the guide's one possibly missable trophy, so read the Positive Mental Attitude entry before the chapter ends.
trophies.name: Paradise Lost

steps.text: Finish every mission in Chapter 1 in story order.
Before the chapter's final mission, check the missables page: one balcony meditation spot only appears during Chapter 1.

trophies.guide: Chapter 2 is a straight story clear: finish its missions in order and the trophy unlocks at the chapter's end. Nothing in this chapter is flagged missable by the sources used here.
trophies.name: T**s Ass Drug Money

steps.text: Play through Chapter 2's missions until the chapter-complete screen shows.
If a mission fails, retry it from the checkpoint; progress toward the chapter is kept.

trophies.guide: The Chapter 3 trophy lands when the chapter's final mission is complete. Keep to the story path; side content can wait until the story is done, because none of it gates this trophy.
trophies.name: Vice City, Baby!

steps.text: Clear Chapter 3's missions in order.
Use the time between missions to try activities, but do not let them pull you off the story for long.

trophies.guide: Chapter 4's trophy is another story clear. By now the mission pace is heavier, so stock up on ammo and armour before the chapter's bigger set pieces rather than mid-mission.
trophies.name: Top Of The World, Ma

steps.text: Finish Chapter 4's missions in order.
Restock between missions so a failed attempt costs a retry, not a long drive back to a shop.

trophies.guide: This gold trophy is the story's ending: finish the final mission and it unlocks with the credits. It is hidden on PlayStation until earned, so the spoiler setting in this guide keeps its name covered until you tick it off.
trophies.name: You Gotta Know When to Get Off

steps.text: Complete Chapters 1 to 4, then take the final mission when it appears.
Play the finale carefully: a failed run restarts at a checkpoint, and the trophy only needs one clean finish.

trophies.guide: Breakfast Run is a named story mission, and finishing it is all this trophy asks. Follow the mission marker when it appears in the story flow; it cannot be skipped or locked out.
trophies.name: Trust

steps.text: Advance the story until the Breakfast Run marker appears, then complete the mission.
Stick to the mission objectives on screen; wandering off the route only wastes time.

trophies.guide: The Cartel Heist is one of the story's big set-piece missions. The trophy needs a single completion, so take the prep seriously: full armour and a ranged loadout make the escape leg far calmer.
trophies.name: Break the Bank

steps.text: Reach The Cartel Heist in the story and finish it.
During the escape, keep moving between cover instead of standing in the open.

trophies.guide: Child's Play is a story mission like the others in this group: complete it and the trophy follows. There is no extra objective hiding behind it, so a normal playthrough earns it.
trophies.name: Family Matters

steps.text: Follow the story to Child's Play and complete the mission.
No collectible or side task is tied to this trophy.

trophies.guide: Headliners is another named story mission. Finish it once and DWNFALL unlocks; like the other story trophies here, it is unmissable as long as you play the story to the end.
trophies.name: DWNFALL

steps.text: Advance the story until Headliners unlocks, then complete it.
If the mission is tough, lower the difficulty in the settings before retrying rather than grinding gear.

trophies.guide: VCIA Takedown is a story mission set around the airport, and one completion unlocks Hi-Jacked. Expect a heavier fight than the early missions, so bring armour and keep a vehicle nearby for the getaway leg.
trophies.name: Hi-Jacked

steps.text: Reach VCIA Takedown in the story and complete the mission.
Use cover inside the terminal area and move in short bursts between objectives.

trophies.guide: Operation Savage Glory is the last of the named story missions in this group. Finish it once for Snow Storm; it sits late in the story, so by the time it appears your loadout should already be strong.
trophies.name: Snow Storm

steps.text: Play the story through to Operation Savage Glory and complete it.
Save before starting, so a failed attempt costs a reload rather than a replay of the approach.

trophies.guide: A Long Road is the 100% completion gold, and it is the real grind behind the platinum: story, stranger strands, collectibles, activities and counts all feed it. Work it last, after the roadmap's other stages, and use the checklist to find the stragglers instead of guessing.
trophies.name: A Long Road

steps.text: Clear the story, all stranger strands and the collectible sets first.
Then sweep the remaining counts in the checklist: stunts, races, challenges and exploration.
The in-game stats page is the honest check of what is still missing; the trophy pops at a true 100%.

trophies.guide: Cunning Stunts counts every stunt you pull off, and 250 is a long tail that builds up across the whole game rather than in one session. The counter in this guide tracks your running total; log stunts in small batches after each play session so the number stays honest.
trophies.name: Cunning Stunts

steps.text: Pull stunts whenever you travel: jumps, near misses and airtime all count.
Use the stepper here to record your total after each session and watch it climb toward 250.
Do not grind it in one sitting; it accumulates naturally while you chase the other trophies.

trophies.description: Try each type of activity once.
trophies.guide: Master of None only asks for one try of each of the 9 activity types, so it is one of the quickest bronzes once you know where the activities live. Sample them early, in stage S3, and tick each type off as you try it.
trophies.name: Master of None

steps.text: Open the activities list in game and try one of each type: racing, fishing, shooting range, bowling, arcade, drone racing and the rest.
A single attempt counts even if you lose, so do not worry about winning any of them.

trophies.description: Earn a gold medal in all Shooting Range challenges.
trophies.guide: The Shootist wants gold in all 42 Shooting Range challenges, which makes it the most skill-gated silver in the set. Treat it as a practice trophy: learn one weapon's rhythm at a time, and use the stepper to record how many challenges are gold so far.
trophies.name: The Shootist

steps.text: Visit the shooting range and work through the challenges weapon by weapon.
Replay a challenge until gold, then move on; silver or bronze does not count.
Record each gold in the stepper so you always know how many of the 42 remain.

trophies.description: Win a Top Fun Drone Race at every location.
trophies.guide: Top Fun runs drone races at 14 locations, and this trophy wants a win at each one. The races are short, so the grind is travel more than skill: clear them location by location and tick each win off in the stepper.
trophies.name: Top Fun

steps.text: Find a Top Fun drone race and win it, then move to the next location.
Learn each course's corners on a practice run before racing for the win.
Count your won locations in the stepper until all 14 are done.

trophies.guide: Twenty different races sounds like a lot until you notice how many race types the map holds. Mix street, off-road and water races rather than repeating one favourite, because only distinct races move the count.
trophies.name: Earn Cash, Not Kudos

steps.text: Enter races of different types and win each one once.
Repeating a race you already won adds nothing, so keep a list of the ones done.
Use the stepper to track the 20 distinct wins.

trophies.description: Beat Cal in a fishing challenge.
trophies.guide: Baited My Tackle is a head-to-head fishing challenge against Cal, and it is more about patience than gear. Watch the line tension, reel in steady bursts, and do not rush the catch when Cal is ahead.
trophies.name: Baited My Tackle

steps.text: Find Cal's fishing challenge and start it.
Keep tension in the safe zone and reel during the calm windows; a snapped line restarts the attempt.

trophies.guide: Stick Fiddler needs one finished arcade game, and any arcade cabinet counts. Pick the shortest game you can find, learn its controls in the first minute, and play it through to the end screen.
trophies.name: Stick Fiddler

steps.text: Walk into an arcade and start any game.
Finish it to its end screen; quitting early does not count.

trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Andy.
trophies.guide: Andy's strand ends with a final mission, and finishing it earns Road to Rehabilitation. Stranger strands unlock as you explore, so if Andy's missions are not appearing, keep playing the story and checking the map for his marker.
trophies.name: Road to Rehabilitation

steps.text: Follow Andy's mission strand from its first marker to its last.
Complete his final mission; earlier missions in the strand do not unlock the trophy on their own.

trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Kenton.
trophies.guide: Kenton's strand works the same way as Andy's: a chain of missions that ends in a finale. Clear each Kenton mission as it appears and the trophy lands on the last one.
trophies.name: This Was No Boat Accident

steps.text: Play through Kenton's missions in order.
Finish his final mission to unlock the trophy.

trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Billy.
trophies.guide: Billy's strand is another mission chain with a finale at the end. Work it in stage S4 alongside the other stranger strands so the map stays tidy and no strand is left half done.
trophies.name: The Lone Rider

steps.text: Follow Billy's strand from the first mission to the last.
Complete the final mission; the trophy does not unlock on earlier missions.

trophies.description: Complete 8 mission strands for strangers across the state of Leonida.
trophies.guide: Strangers & Freaks is the umbrella over the side strands: finish 8 full stranger mission chains across Leonida. The named strands for Andy, Kenton, Billy, Randy and Tyrone already cover five, so three more stranger chains finish it.
trophies.name: Strangers & Freaks

steps.text: Complete the stranger strands for Andy, Kenton, Billy, Randy and Tyrone.
Find three more stranger chains on the map and finish each one fully.
Track finished strands in the stepper until you reach 8.

trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Randy.
trophies.guide: Randy's strand ends like the others: a final mission that unlocks Supply & Demand when complete. Keep his marker on your route during stage S4 so his chain does not stall halfway.
trophies.name: Supply & Demand

steps.text: Play Randy's missions in order as they appear.
Complete his final mission for the trophy.

trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Tyrone.
trophies.guide: Tyrone's strand is the last of the five named stranger chains in this guide. Finish his missions in order and the finale unlocks Spin On This!; it also counts toward the 8 strands of Strangers & Freaks.
trophies.name: Spin On This!

steps.text: Follow Tyrone's strand through to its final mission.
Complete the finale; it counts as one of the 8 strands for the silver.

trophies.description: Meditate at every spot across Leonida.
trophies.guide: Positive Mental Attitude wants a meditation at all 18 spots across Leonida, and it is the one trophy this guide flags as possibly missable: one balcony meditation spot is only reachable during Chapter 1, before that chapter's story moves on. Do the balcony spot first, while Chapter 1 is still open, then sweep the other 17 spots at your own pace. The stepper tracks how many spots you have meditated at.
trophies.name: Positive Mental Attitude

steps.text: During Chapter 1, go to the balcony meditation spot and meditate there before the chapter ends.
After that, visit each remaining meditation spot across Leonida and meditate once at each.
Record each spot in the stepper until all 18 are done.

trophies.description: Hunt a unique animal for Bret.
trophies.guide: Fair Game sends you after one unique animal for Bret. This is a single-source trophy in this guide, so treat the location as a lead rather than a certainty: scout the hunting area first, track the animal patiently, and take the shot only when you have a clear line.
trophies.name: Fair Game

steps.text: Pick up Bret's hunt and head to the hunting grounds it points to.
Track the unique animal quietly and take it down in one clean attempt.

trophies.guide: Don't Touch My Deck needs three full collectible card sets, so the work is finding cards, not fighting. Cards are scattered across the map; collect in sweeps by district and tick each set off when it completes.
trophies.name: Don't Touch My Deck

steps.text: Search districts in order and pick up every card you pass.
A set only counts when every card in it is found, so finish one set before starting the next.
Track completed sets in the stepper until you reach 3.

trophies.guide: You WAiNKer! is a 100-location sweep: use the WAiNK feature at each spot on the list. It pairs naturally with exploration, so do it while you are already travelling for the other collectible trophies and let the stepper carry the count.
trophies.name: You WAiNKer!

steps.text: At each WAiNK location, use the feature once and move on.
Sweep district by district so no location is visited twice by mistake.
Record each new location in the stepper toward 100.

trophies.guide: One Last Thing counts 50 completed challenges of any kind. Challenges overlap with almost everything else in this guide, so most of the 50 will already be done by the time you reach stage S5; finish the remainder by picking the shortest challenge types left.
trophies.name: One Last Thing

steps.text: Play normally and let challenges complete alongside the other trophies.
Near the end, open the challenge list and clear the quickest unfinished ones.
Track the total in the stepper until it hits 50.

trophies.description: Lose a 4 star Wanted Level with your partner and escape the heat.
trophies.guide: Hot Together needs a 4-star wanted level, lost while your partner is with you, followed by a clean escape. This is flagged as watch in this guide: the partner must be present for the whole escape, so set it up deliberately rather than hoping it happens by accident.
trophies.name: Hot Together

steps.text: Bring your partner along, then raise heat until you hit 4 stars.
Break line of sight and stay hidden until the wanted level clears with your partner still beside you.

trophies.description: Rob 3 shops back-to-back with your partner without losing your Wanted Level.
trophies.guide: Retail Therapy is three shop robberies in a row, with your partner, without the wanted level dropping in between. It is flagged watch because the chain breaks if the heat clears: plan a route with three close shops, hit them fast, and keep the wanted level alive between stops.
trophies.name: Retail Therapy

steps.text: Pick three shops close together and bring your partner.
Rob them one after another without letting the wanted level clear between robberies.

trophies.guide: Whip It Good counts each new vehicle you discover, up to 100. It builds up fast if you drive something different every time you travel instead of defaulting to one car; the stepper keeps the running total.
trophies.name: Whip It Good

steps.text: Drive a different vehicle type whenever you travel: cars, bikes, boats and more.
Each first-time discovery counts, so variety matters more than distance.
Log new discoveries in the stepper toward 100.

trophies.description: Take down 5 enemies in a single use of Combat Focus.
trophies.guide: Gunslinger is one clean Combat Focus: five enemies down before it ends. Set it up on purpose: find a group of enemies close together, trigger Combat Focus, and work through them fast instead of waiting for a random firefight to line up.
trophies.name: Gunslinger

steps.text: Find a spot where five or more enemies stand close together.
Trigger Combat Focus and take all five down before it runs out.

trophies.description: Make an unscheduled departure at VCIA.
trophies.guide: Catch Me If You Can is about leaving the airport on your own terms: an unscheduled departure from VCIA. This is a single-source trophy here, so treat the exact method as a lead: get to the airport, find a way out by air, and leave without following the normal exit.
trophies.name: Catch Me If You Can

steps.text: Head to VCIA and look for an aircraft you can take.
Depart by air without using the scheduled route.

trophies.guide: Challenging Tank is the Rhino trophy, and the sources used here disagree on the exact setup, so this guide marks it as disagree: expect a tank encounter and improvise from the official description rather than trusting one method. Bring heavy weapons and a fast vehicle for the aftermath.
trophies.name: Challenging Tank

steps.text: Find a Rhino tank encounter and engage it as the description suggests.
If one approach fails, try another: the sources differ, so no single method is certain.

trophies.description: Rob a jewelry store without being detected.
trophies.guide: Sneakthief is a stealth robbery: one jewelry store, no detection. This is a single-source trophy, so plan from the description itself: go in quiet, move slowly, take what you came for, and leave before anyone raises the alarm.
trophies.name: Sneakthief

steps.text: Enter the jewelry store quietly and avoid the staff's line of sight.
Take the goods and slip out before any alarm goes up.

trophies.guide: Maximum Withdrawal is five bank vault robberies, each with a clean escape. Plan each vault like a small heist: know the exit before you go in, and do not linger for extra loot once the vault is open.
trophies.name: Maximum Withdrawal

steps.text: Rob a bank vault and escape to safety.
Repeat at four more vaults, tracking each completed robbery in the stepper.
A failed escape does not count, so only a clean getaway moves the total.

trophies.description: Rob an Armored Truck and escape.
trophies.guide: A Classic Blitz Play is one armored truck robbery with a clean escape. It is the classic GTA-style hit in miniature: stop the truck, take the cash, and lose the heat before it builds. A fast getaway car parked nearby makes the escape leg easy.
trophies.name: A Classic Blitz Play

steps.text: Find an armored truck on the road and stop it.
Take the cash and escape before the wanted level climbs.

trophies.guide: The Goodtime State wants all 52 areas of Leonida explored. It pairs perfectly with the collectible sweeps: every district you visit for cards, WAiNK spots and meditation counts here too, so finish it during stage S5 rather than as a separate chore.
trophies.name: The Goodtime State

steps.text: Travel through every district of Leonida, including the outskirts.
Use the stepper to record how many of the 52 areas you have covered.
Combine this with the card and WAiNK sweeps to avoid backtracking.

trophies.description: Rob an Illegal Operation belonging to each gang.
trophies.guide: Pest Control wants one illegal operation robbed from each of the 9 gangs. It is a tour of Leonida's underworld: hit a different gang's operation each time and tick the gangs off in the stepper as you go.
trophies.name: Pest Control

steps.text: Find an illegal operation run by one gang and rob it.
Repeat for each of the other 8 gangs, one operation per gang.
Track the gangs covered in the stepper until all 9 are done.

trophies.description: Enjoy a cocktail with a view on Ocean Beach.
trophies.guide: In The Beginning… is a quiet one: a cocktail with a view on Ocean Beach. It is flagged watch in this guide only because it is easy to walk past: go to the beachfront, order the cocktail, and enjoy the view until the trophy pops. It also disagrees across sources on the exact spot, so try the main beachfront first.
trophies.name: In The Beginning…

steps.text: Go to Ocean Beach and find the beachfront bar spot.
Order a cocktail and stay for the view until the trophy unlocks.

trophies.description: Smash your way out of a vehicle showroom in classic style.
trophies.guide: Capital Offense is the showroom smash: drive out through the glass in classic style. It is flagged watch because the setup matters more than the smash itself: pick a showroom with a clear exit line, build speed inside, and go straight through.
trophies.name: Capital Offense

steps.text: Drive into a vehicle showroom and line up an exit through the front.
Smash out through the glass in one run.

trophies.description: Follow-through at the Kolt & Associates' bowling alley.
trophies.guide: Let's Go Bowling is a visit to the Kolt & Associates bowling alley with a proper follow-through. It is flagged watch only because the alley is easy to miss on the map: find the alley, bowl a game, and follow through on the lane.
trophies.name: Let’s Go Bowling

steps.text: Find the Kolt & Associates bowling alley.
Bowl a full game with a proper follow-through.

trophies.guide: Personal Best is one of the vaguest descriptions on the official list, and this guide marks it unconfirmed: the description alone does not pin down what to do. The honest approach is to keep playing with your partner and watch for a partnership moment that the game itself celebrates.
trophies.name: Personal Best

steps.text: Play partner activities and look for a moment the game frames as a shared success.
No step here is verified in the game yet, so treat any specific claim about it with caution.

trophies.guide: Actions Speak Louder is the choices trophy: PSN tracks a count up to 500, so it rewards a long habit of making choices rather than one big decision. It is unconfirmed in this guide because the description does not say which choices count; keep choosing, keep playing, and let the count build.
trophies.name: Actions Speak Louder

steps.text: Make choices whenever the game offers them, across missions and free roam.
The count climbs over time; there is no shortcut to 500 in one session.

trophies.guide: Bad Luck, I Guess is the second-try trophy: succeed where you once failed. It is flagged watch because the trigger is a retry, not a first attempt: when something fails, go back and clear it on the second try instead of moving on.
trophies.name: Bad Luck, I Guess

steps.text: When an activity or mission fails, retry it right away.
Succeed on the second attempt to unlock the trophy.

trophies.guide: The Truth Is Out There is the strange-encounter trophy: witness something odd in Leonida. It is unconfirmed and single-source in this guide, because the description gives no place and no trigger. Explore odd corners of the map, especially at night, and let the weird find you.
trophies.name: The Truth Is Out There

steps.text: Explore unusual spots across Leonida, particularly away from the main roads.
The trigger is not verified, so this one may take patience.

trophies.description: Bowl 'em over with a melee drive-by.
trophies.guide: Ten Pin is a melee drive-by: knock someone down from a moving vehicle with a melee attack. The sources disagree on the exact setup, so this guide marks it as disagree: try it at low speed first, aim for a single target, and repeat until the hit registers.
trophies.name: Ten Pin

steps.text: Drive slowly past a target with a melee weapon ready.
Strike during the drive-by and knock the target over.

trophies.description: Earn $250,000 laundering Marked Bills through your contacts.
trophies.guide: Dime on the Dollar is the laundering grind: $250,000 of marked bills cleaned through your contacts. It is pure money work in stage S7, so stack marked bills during the crime stages and launder them in batches; the stepper tracks the running total.
trophies.name: Dime on the Dollar

steps.text: Collect marked bills from robberies and heists.
Launder them through your contacts in batches and record the total in the stepper.
Keep going until $250,000 is laundered.

trophies.guide: Treat Yo Self is the spending trophy: $100,000 across all shops. It happens almost by itself if you buy gear, ammo and vehicles through the game, but the stepper lets you check the total if it is the last money trophy standing.
trophies.name: Treat Yo Self

steps.text: Buy gear, ammo, clothes and vehicles from shops as you play.
Record your spending in the stepper until it reaches $100,000.

trophies.guide: Little Boxes wants all 8 garage properties bought. This is a single-source trophy here, so buy garages as your money allows and check the property list after each purchase so none is missed. It pairs with the money trophies in stage S7.
trophies.name: Little Boxes

steps.text: Buy garage properties one by one as you can afford them.
Track the purchases in the stepper until all 8 are owned.

trophies.description: Register 10 vehicles to the Scooter Bros app.
trophies.guide: On the Spot is the last money-adjacent trophy: register 10 vehicles to the Scooter Bros app. Find vehicles around the map, open the app, and register each one; the stepper counts them up to 10.
trophies.name: On the Spot

steps.text: Find a vehicle and open the Scooter Bros app.
Register the vehicle, then repeat with nine more different vehicles.
Track the registrations in the stepper until you reach 10.
